Hello Dear EarthLings!

We are a team of 2 space-healthcare enthusiasts:

Khanak Kukreja- Co-Founder of FutureDR.Ca, Neuroscience Research Intern

Shikha Kukreja- a dentist, learning and development professional in healthcare and the Co-Founder of FutureDR.Ca

- Future DR.G⁰ Team
summary:
DR. G⁰ is a dynamic health monitoring system designed to track astronauts’ blood pressure, oxygen levels, heart rate, temperature, sleep duration and consistency, activity and exercise, and daily mood. It presents both formal charts and graphs and simplified, scannable summaries—because our astronauts study the universe, not EEG graphs! When measurements are unusually high, DR. G⁰ alerts connected devices that medical assistance may be needed. It also maintains a full medical history.

However, medical emergencies can occur despite taking every precaution. With communication to Earth taking up to 20 minutes per side and CMOs often receiving only basic training, we developed G⁰ Emergency. Astronauts can search their medical concerns to receive descriptive guides generated using Natural Health Resources and NASA's emergency training modules, helping them handle emergencies or prevent them altogether.

Beyond daily health check-ups, DR. G⁰ supports astronaut entertainment through AstroPlay, mental health through MindSpace's guided breathing sessions and journaling, and connection to Earth through the EarthLing chatbot.

Our astronauts help keep Earth safe while risking themselves. DR. G⁰ helps protect their health, prevent isolation and distance from loved ones, and manage emergencies regardless of their medical experience.
details:
Problem

Every time we think about space, we often picture spaceships, stars, and astronauts- but when we dig beyond the surface level, we realise that all this exciting stuff isn't the most fun when it attacks your health every second- that’s how it is for our astronauts.

In nearly every spaceflight the 3 most common health risks are:

  • Heart & Blood Vessels: Blood vessels stiffen and age faster, and astronauts can develop insulin resistance, which may lead to Type 2 diabetes. These factors increase the risk of cardiovascular disease.
  • Muscles & Nervous System: Muscles lose mass and strength. Reflexes slow down and exercise tends to be less effective in space.
  • Mental Health Challenges: One of the easiest to overlook, yet incredibly impactful. Being hundreds and thousands of kilometers away from home, family, and safety is one of the most daunting feelings, causing severe anxiety and depression. These factors impact a crew member’s sleep, morale, and decision making.

Ideation/ Vision/ Factors We Considered

  • We knew we wanted our project to take care of our crew members both physically and mentally because being in the middle of nowhere is both hard on the bones and brains.
  • We also realized that we should focus on: Prevention and Handling Emergencies
  • Prevention: Because conducting surgeries in extremely difficult in space- it’s important to focus on avoiding and preventing any medical complication in the first place by using natural health solutions that have been clinically backed to support health in zero gravity
  • Handling Emergencies: No matter how much one avoids complications- it’s important to be equipped with the necessary skills and knowledge to handle any complications. However, with communication delays for up to 20 mins each side, connecting with earth may not be the fastest solution- so we’d like to consider a solution to create onsite support for crew members.

Solution

  • We made a dynamic health monitoring system which tracks a crew member's: blood pressure, oxygen level, heart rate, temperature, sleep(duration and consistency), activity and exercise, and daily mood!
  • Provides both formal charts and graphs, as well as simplified scannable summaries- because our astronauts study the universe, not EEG graphs!
  • Alerts connected device when a certain measurement is unusually high and may need medical assistance 
  • However, many medical emergencies can take place despite doing everything in our control. In these cases, communication with earth can take up to 20 mins./side, and CMOs are often only given basic training.
  • To help out with this, we created G⁰ Emergency- astronauts type their problem in the search engine, and we use Natural Health Resources and NASA’s Emergency training modules to create descriptive guides when handling emergencies or simply preventing them
  • Aside from daily health checks-up, DR. G⁰ also takes care of our astronaut entertainment with AstroPlay, mental health with MindSpace’s guided breathing session, journal and EarthLing chat bot
  • This health monitoring system keeps the crew in good shape, health, a strong connection to earth and their families and keeps them in a good mood.

How is each problem tackled? Research

Heart & Blood Vessels- G⁰ Emergency Solutions:

  • Nadi Shodhana (Alternate Nostril Breathing): Slowing the breath and alternating nostrils stimulates the vagus nerve and balances the autonomic nervous system. Clinical trials prove it lowers systolic/diastolic blood pressure, reduces resting heart rate, and improves arterial elasticity and insulin sensitivity. 
  • Humming breath (Bhramari Pranayama): Research in the American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine shows that humming vibrations boost natural nitric oxide production by 15-fold, signaling stiff arterial walls to relax- restoring healthy blood flow. At the same time, clinical trials confirm that just five minutes of humming stimulates the vagus nerve to trigger an immediate drop in blood pressure and resting heart rate, while daily practice lowers stress hormones, fasting blood glucose, and insulin resistance, protecting astronauts' cardiovascular health on deep-space missions without adding any medical payload.

Muscles & Nervous System- G⁰ Emergency Solutions: 

  • Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) is a clinically validated adaptogenic root extract evaluated in aerospace pharmacology (Life Sciences in Space Research, 2026) as a low-mass countermeasure against microgravity-induced muscle atrophy. In weightlessness, mechanical unloading, radiation-driven oxidative stress, and elevated myostatin accelerate skeletal muscle breakdown. Double-blind clinical trials demonstrate that standardized Ashwagandha suppresses myostatin and inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, hs-CRP), boosts cellular antioxidant glutathione (GSH), and activates IGF-1/Akt/mTOR protein synthesis—measurably increasing muscle mass and strength without adding heavy gym payload to deep-space spacecraft.
  • Utkatasana: In NASA’s simulated-microgravity bed-rest trials, researchers tested high-intensity squat and calf-press resistance exercises during prolonged unloading. While non-exercising bed-rest controls lost 14% of their lower-limb muscle mass in 10 days, subjects performing high-load squat and calf contractions preserved 100% of thigh (1757 ± 222 cm³ to 1771 ± 240 cm³) and calf (622 ± 195 cm³ to 628 ± 202 cm³) muscle volume over 14 days, and offset 100% of quadriceps mass loss and ~67% of soleus (calf) mass loss over 70 days. Biomechanically, this exact high-tension squat and calf-loading movement is very similar to Utkatasana (Chair Pose) paired with isometric calf holds; allowing astronauts to reproduce the same lower-limb muscle recruitment using a simple foot strap when bulky gym machines cannot fit on deep-space capsules.

Mental Health Challenges

  • MindSpace:
    • Journaling: NASA recommended Journal for each astronaut
    • Meditation Hubs: Various Meditation Centers in app
    • HummingVerse: Known to help reduce stress levels
    • Talk to a Fellow EarthLing: Provides a sense of belonging
    • CrewKaraoke: Encourages teamwork, and allows for creative freedom
    • CrewCharades: Encourages teamwork, and allows for creative freedom

Future Uses and Benefits

  • Enabling Autonomous Medical Procedures in Space: DR. G⁰ establishes a foundational framework for future surgeries in space, enabling crew members to independently perform medical procedures without relying on constant communication or real-time guidance from Earth.
  • Supporting Future Deep-Space Missions: DR. G⁰'s autonomous emergency-response capabilities could support missions such as NASA's Mars Sample Return (MSR), whose timeline and costs increased significantly partly due to the complexity of prolonged deep-space operations. By reducing reliance on Earth-based communication and empowering crews to independently manage emergencies, our system could help streamline mission operations, reduce communication-related delays, and support more efficient, autonomous exploration.
